name: Axiom Systems Portable Diaspora Terminal PDT-4
product_name: Axiom Systems Portable Diaspora Terminal PDT-4
description: A ruggedized portable terminal that provides Diaspora network access in areas without infrastructure coverage. The PDT-4 establishes a satellite uplink and creates a local wireless hotspot serving up to 50 users within a 100-meter radius. Axiom deploys them in emergency situations and sells them to organizations operating in infrastructure-poor zones. The terminal includes content filtering consistent with Axiom's Automated Censorship Infrastructure, ensuring that even off-grid Diaspora access operates within Axiom's information control parameters.
story_hooks: A PDT-4 deployed in a Tier 1 dead zone has been modified to bypass the ACI content filter — for the first time, residents are accessing unfiltered Diaspora and discovering how much information has been hidden from them.

Axiom is distributing free PDT-4 terminals in underserved districts as a humanitarian gesture — but each terminal maps every device that connects to it, building a comprehensive census of the off-grid population.

physical_description.visual_profile: A ruggedized briefcase-style terminal with a distinctly utilitarian military-industrial aesthetic. The PDT-4 resembles a hardened communications device from the early 2200s, featuring a boxy, angular form factor designed for durability over aesthetics. The top surface slopes slightly and includes a recessed satellite antenna array that deploys vertically when powered on.
physical_description.weight_description: 3 kg — handheld but substantial; typically carried with reinforced carry handle or shoulder strap; deployable on a workbench or tripod mount
physical_description.primary_material: Titanium-reinforced polycarbonate composite chassis with magnesium alloy frame
physical_description.finish: Textured matte gunmetal gray with micro-perforated ventilation panels; sealed against environmental ingress (IP67 rated)
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary body with charcoal accent panels; white LED indicators; Φ-branded blue accent lighting around perimeter when active
physical_description.interface_elements: Top-mounted 12cm monochrome LCD status display (showing signal strength, user count, bandwidth allocation); four recessed tactile buttons (power, mode select, emergency reset, diagnostic); dual USB-C ports (data/charging) on right side; status LED cluster (power, satellite lock, network activity, thermal warning) positioned above display; integrated heatsink vents along back edge
distinctive_features: Deployable satellite antenna array (4 phased elements) that rises 8cm from center-top when powered; retracts flush when dormant
Axiom Systems corporate sigil embossed in chrome on lower right corner
Emergency manual release keyhole for content filter override (physical failsafe)
Subtle etched regulatory compliance matrix (FCC, GLMZ authorities, Axiom ACI certification) on back panel
Cooling fins on rear housing — terminal runs hot under sustained load
Faint holographic security seal on battery compartment showing Axiom anti-tampering verification
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: AXIOM SYSTEMS in sans-serif block capitals across top bezel; PDT-4 model designation above LCD; manufacturing date code and serial number on lower left; regulatory stamps (GLMZ 2226 certification, Diaspora compliance authority approval) on rear
physical_description.condition_typical: When deployed in field, antenna array is fully extended; LED indicators glow soft blue (network active) or amber (searching for satellite); used units show scuff marks, impact adhesive patches, and weathering on edges; units in high-use infrastructure-poor zones accumulate dust in ventilation grilles; antenna tips occasionally show minor corrosion from environmental exposure
